messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: deploy-canary-fail for service `resp-runner` in us-west-2. 3/5 canary instances reporting 500s, error spike detected at 11:42 UTC.
Deploy-bot: CI pipeline #2847 finished deploy to canary (tag: `latest`) - rollout started at 11:40 UTC. Link: https://ci.redwood/inv/2847
Emma S: seeing alerts too. grafana shows error rate jump from 0.2% -> 6% at 11:42. Canary only (2/5 replicas failing).
Raj K: I kicked off that canary. I used the image tag from the pipeline which is `latest` here. looking into registry.
Sofia P: ugh `latest` again? we explicitly asked to use immutable tags in the release playbook.
Raj K: digging into the CI logs, build step used `docker build -t registry.redwood/resp-runner:latest .` then `docker push registry.redwood/resp-runner:latest`. No digest recorded in the deploy manifest.
Tilly Ops: can we flip the feature flag / kill-switch for canary routing? feature `new-routing` gates the new code path.
Emma S: yes please, toggle `new-routing` off for service resp-runner-canary. That should immediate-route traffic back to stable path.
Maya SRE: I'm taking the pager handoff—oncall now. estimating customer impact. Any sign of data corruption or cache poisoning?
Ben P: looking at pod logs: stacktrace shows KV cache deserialization error in the hot path. 500s originate from a new codepath that assumes a different cache schema. Doesn't look like persistent data loss but clients hitting canary saw errors.
Sofia P: ok so code mismatch with cached payloads, likely introduced by the canary build. Good we didn't ramp more.
Tilly Ops: toggled flag -> `new-routing: false` via /flagship API. Response: 200 OK. :white_check_mark:
Deploy-bot: Rollout pause triggered by canary failure. Canary replicas left at 5, no further promotion.
Raj K: prepared a rollback to previous image digest. running: 
```
kubectl -n prod set image deploy/resp-runner resp-runner=registry.redwood/resp-runner@sha256:4a7f8c2 --record
```
Executing now.
Emma S: after rollback, error rate dropping in canary within 30s. still watching.
Maya SRE: customer impact: estimated ~1200 requests failed across canary during 11:42-11:50 window. primary customer-facing services unaffected (traffic routed to stable for most tenants). Notifying CS to prepare possible emails for a few enterprise tenants that hit the canary.
Ben P: root cause hypothesis: CI job used mutable `latest` tag and a subsequent rebuild (different commit) reused the same tag due to a parallel pipeline race, which ended up deploying an incompatible artifact. We also saw docker registry return manifest for `latest` that didn't match the deploy's expected sha.
Sofia P: that matches local repro: pushing the same `latest` tag from two different commits happened during a backfill earlier. Our pipeline allows `latest` mutability.
Raj K: next steps I'm taking now: 1) confirm rollback completed and all canaries serving previous digest 2) backfill canary logs into audit 3) open PR to force digest pinning in deploy manifests.
Tilly Ops: also adding a short-lived kill-switch in the routing service to drop canary traffic if healthscore < 90%.
Maya SRE: I'm going to escalate to a full incident ticket and assign postmortem owner. Owner: Raj K. Severity: sev2 (partial degradation, limited tenants).
Emma S: notified #support and added a note for CS: "Canary transient failures during deploy; we rolled back; monitoring shows recovery. We'll follow up with root cause and mitigation." :eyes:
Raj K: creating followup tasks: 
- enforce immutable tags in CI (push digest + tag, deploy by digest)
- add CI invariant that prevents pushing `latest` without commit SHA suffix
- release pipeline change to record image digest into deployment artifact store
- postmortem + timeline doc (owner: me, due EOD tomorrow)
Sofia P: also recommend a small change to canary gating: verify cache schema compatibility before routing traffic (small canary bootstrap check).
Ben P: confirming no sign of cache poisoning beyond schema mismatch — cache entries look valid, just different shapes. still need to hardened schema checks.
Maya SRE: policies for customer comms: CS to wait for postmortem before broad outbound, but flag potentially impacted tenants for heads-up.
Emma S: thanks everyone. great quick response. handoff: Raj remains owner for followups, I'm continuing monitoring. :thumbsup:
